docs.text: Pulsar Python SDK

docs.title: Lifecycle and recovery
docs.text: Operating state, connection state, and health are separate facts. Use Actuator.status and GroupStatus rather than inferring safety from one boolean.

docs.title: Operating states
docs.text:
State Meaning UNKNOWN disconnected or not observed; cannot be requested INIT_CONFIG output and runtime telemetry inactive; configuration allowed CONFIG_AND_TELEM telemetry active; drive output inactive DRIVE_ACTIVE commands can affect output

A successful connection ends in INIT_CONFIG. configure() and set_mode() are allowed only in INIT_CONFIG or CONFIG_AND_TELEM; neither enables output. sync() first enters CONFIG_AND_TELEM where needed, then resets telemetry timing for the whole domain.

enable() requires a complete configuration, checks current diagnostics, synchronizes the domain when required, and enters DRIVE_ACTIVE. disable() returns to CONFIG_AND_TELEM, where telemetry remains available while output is inactive.

zero_position() is allowed in CONFIG_AND_TELEM or DRIVE_ACTIVE. In position and impedance modes, the SDK also resets the primary command to zero to avoid sudden motion. Changing mode clears the primary command and command-scoped feedforward or impedance references; configured gains remain in place.

docs.title: Status
docs.text:
Actuator.status reports:

  • current and last observed operating state;
  • connection state;
  • HEALTHY, HOST_FAULT, or ACTUATOR_FAULT;
  • retained device diagnostics and host errors;
  • the last safety attempt;
  • peer inhibition;
  • recommended recovery action.

docs.title: Default controller safety
docs.text:
The default ControllerErrorPolicy selects a mode-specific action:

Mode Default action position hold an available position; otherwise zero and command zero impedance hold position; otherwise damped release velocity command zero velocity torque enter output-inactive state, switch to velocity, re-enable through the safety path, and command zero velocity

If the selected action fails, the default fallback requests INIT_CONFIG. Command-based hold, damping, and zero-command actions are best effort because they have no operation-specific device acknowledgement.

Safety applies only while output is active. Diagnostics received while output is inactive are retained and checked before a later enable, but they do not energize output or send active hold commands.

docs.title: Device diagnostics
docs.text:
Named DiagnosticFlag values are exposed instead of raw bit positions.

Default behavior includes:

  • overtemperature → torque derating;
  • internal or external encoder error → INIT_CONFIG;
  • other unmapped errors → default safety;
  • unmapped warnings → reported and logged without automatic safety.

An unexpected observed state change pauses the owning group and propagates safety to reachable group peers and, when present, other platform groups. Operations across actuators and domains are not atomic.

Mode-dependent command safety is applied only while output is active. Diagnostics received while output is inactive are retained and checked before a later enable, but they do not send hold or damping commands, switch modes, or energize output.

docs.title: Recovery sequences
docs.text:
Situation Action Connection lost reconnect; the previous physical state is unknown Stale telemetry or controller fault fix the cause, call clear_faults(), then resume() Diagnostic handled while output remains active wait for it to clear, call clear_faults(), then resume() if paused Diagnostic safety entered INIT_CONFIG clear the physical condition, call recover(), then resume() or enable()

clear_faults() verifies current diagnostics and returns False while a mapped condition remains active. recover() is only for diagnostic safety that selected INIT_CONFIG; it is not a general host-fault clear operation.

docs.title: Advanced policies
docs.text:
ControllerErrorPolicy, diagnostic action mappings, damping, and explicit diagnostic overrides are documented in the API reference.

Danger

ControllerErrorAction.DO_NOTHING and override_diagnostic_safety() can suppress automatic safety behavior. Use them only for a controlled, reviewed application with an independent safety plan.

docs.title: Connection loss and shutdown
docs.text:
After transport loss, the SDK reports UNKNOWN and preserves the previous observation in status.last_operating_state. It does not claim that unreachable hardware is safe.

Explicit physical disconnect attempts to reach and observe INIT_CONFIG before releasing the transport. It raises when the SDK cannot confirm that state. Do not rely on Python object destruction for hardware safety; use disable() and disconnect(), or a context manager.

docs.title: Telemetry and callbacks
docs.text: Pulsar Python SDK

docs.title: Telemetry and callbacks
docs.text: Pulsar Python SDK supports direct telemetry reads, actuator callbacks, complete group controller batches, and platform-wide callback registration.

docs.title: Configure periodic telemetry
docs.text:
from pulsar_sdk import ControlConfiguration, Mode, TelemetryItems

configuration = ControlConfiguration(
    mode=Mode.POSITION,
    telemetry_items=(
        TelemetryItems.POSITION,
        TelemetryItems.VELOCITY,
        TelemetryItems.TIMESTAMP_MS,
    ),
    telemetry_rate_hz=500,
)

At most 12 unique telemetry items may be configured. The effective rate is available as actual_telemetry_rate_hz.

docs.title: Read a snapshot
docs.text:
telemetry = actuator.read_telemetry((
    TelemetryItems.POSITION,
    TelemetryItems.VELOCITY,
))

Snapshot reads are available in CONFIG_AND_TELEM or DRIVE_ACTIVE.

docs.title: Actuator callback
docs.text:
def on_telemetry(address, telemetry):
    print(address, telemetry[TelemetryItems.POSITION])

actuator.set_telemetry_callback(on_telemetry)

One worker per execution domain runs user callbacks away from the transport reader thread. For each callback source, at most one callback runs and one newest pending packet waits. Older pending work may be replaced; inspect dropped_telemetry_packets.

docs.title: Group controller
docs.text:
A group controller runs after one new sample has arrived from every member:

from pulsar_sdk import ControlParams


def controller(metadata, telemetry):
    return {
        name: {ControlParams.COMMAND: values[TelemetryItems.POSITION]}
        for name, values in telemetry.items()
    }

arm.set_control_callback(controller)

Callback output is fully validated before the first member write. Member writes are sequential, so a later transport failure can occur after an earlier command was sent. Callback-path transmission failures latch a HostError and apply the configured safety policy.

If the source is stopped, reconfigured, or faulted while the callback runs, its result is discarded. Inspect dropped_batches when newer complete group batches replace pending work.

docs.title: Platform callback
docs.text: Platform.set_control_callback() registers the same callback on every group. Calls remain independent, may run on different domain workers, and use metadata.group_name to identify the source. A platform does not create one cross-domain telemetry batch or synchronize domain clocks.

docs.title: Timeouts
docs.text:
An ActuatorGroup has two independent timeouts:

  • telemetry_timeout_s, default 0.1 seconds;
  • controller_timeout_s, default 1.0 second, or None to disable the callback deadline.

The telemetry timeout applies only while callback control is active and periodic telemetry is configured. Stale telemetry or a callback deadline pauses callback control and applies the configured safety policy. Fresh telemetry alone does not clear the retained fault or resume control; fix the cause, call clear_faults(), then call resume().

Python cannot cancel a callback thread that exceeds its deadline. Its eventual result is discarded.

docs.title: Removing callbacks
docs.text: Removing a callback from another thread waits for its current invocation to finish. A diagnostic callback cannot replace itself while running; doing so raises ResourceBusyError.

docs.text: Pulsar Python SDK

docs.title: Virtual actuators
docs.text: PulsarActuatorVirtual runs a validated AUGUR Digital Twin actuator model inside a VirtualWorld.

docs.title: Install assets
docs.text:
Install Pixi first. The following commands are identical on Linux and Windows:

pixi workspace channel add --prepend https://prefix.dev/pulsarhri/pulsar-forge
pixi add pulsar-sdk pulsar-assets

List models available on the current host:

pixi run pulsar-cli virtual-scan

Supported models are:

  • P90
  • P100
  • PULSE98-30G
  • PULSE98-55G
  • PULSE115-60G
  • PULSE115-110G

docs.title: Create a world and actuator
docs.text:
from pulsar_sdk import PulsarActuatorVirtual, VirtualWorld

world = VirtualWorld()
actuator = PulsarActuatorVirtual(
    world,
    model="PULSE115-60G",
    address=1,
)

Without an explicit assets_path, lookup checks PULSAR_ASSETS_PATH and then active Conda/Python environment asset locations.

docs.title: Configure and step
docs.text:
from pulsar_sdk import ControlConfiguration, Mode, TelemetryItems

with actuator:
    actuator.configure(
        ControlConfiguration(
            Mode.POSITION,
            (TelemetryItems.POSITION, TelemetryItems.VELOCITY),
            500,
        )
    )
    actuator.enable()
    actuator.set_command(0.5)

    for _ in range(100):
        world.step()

    actuator.disable()

VirtualWorld.step():

  1. finds the earliest next periodic telemetry event among connected virtual actuators;
  2. applies supplied loads for the required internal model ticks;
  3. advances connected models in registration order;
  4. delivers due telemetry;
  5. waits for due actuator and group callbacks;
  6. returns after callback commands are stored for the next public step.

If periodic telemetry is disabled, one call advances one 50 µs internal tick. Disconnected actuators do not participate in stepping and cannot stop other models in the world.

docs.title: External loads
docs.text:
world.step(loads_by_address={1: 0.25})

Loads are finite output-shaft torques in N·m keyed by connected virtual actuator address. Positive load opposes positive output motion.

docs.title: Passive states
docs.text:
In INIT_CONFIG and CONFIG_AND_TELEM, the virtual plant remains mechanically movable under external load but produces passive zero torque. Telemetry is unavailable in INIT_CONFIG, matching physical lifecycle behavior. DRIVE_ACTIVE restores the configured control mode.

Telemetry staleness uses simulation time, so pausing the application or debugger does not fault a world that is not advancing. Raw or device-only telemetry is unsupported; virtual BUS_VOLTAGE reports the model's fixed 48 V supply.

Position reset occurs on one world-owned 50 µs tick. Every connected actuator advances on that tick, and members of one group reset together.

docs.title: Asset isolation
docs.text:
Each actuator instance loads an isolated copy of its generated model library because generated models contain process-global state.

For robot dynamics and simulator ownership, read Co-simulation coupling.

docs.title: Physical actuators
docs.text:
PulsarActuatorReal controls a physical PULSE actuator through a PCP execution domain.

Choose:

  • Direct USB for one actuator at address 0.
  • CAN for one or more actuators with unique addresses.

docs.title: Common workflow
docs.text:
from pulsar_sdk import ControlConfiguration, Mode, PulsarActuatorReal

actuator = PulsarActuatorReal(domain, address)
with actuator:
    actuator.configure(ControlConfiguration(Mode.POSITION))
    actuator.enable()
    actuator.set_command(0.0)
    actuator.disable()

Physical state transitions complete only after the requested state is observed. After communication loss, the SDK reports UNKNOWN rather than assuming the previous state is still safe.

CAN addresses must be unique within one PcpOverCan domain and lie in 16..16382. Direct USB supports one actuator at address 0.

Address change, identify, parameter persistence, bootloader entry, and CAN bit-rate switching are physical-only capabilities. Check supports() or the returned FeatureResult instead of assuming every transport provides them. Operations without dedicated firmware acknowledgement may report UNCONFIRMED.

Physical actuator firmware must be 2.0.4 or newer.

docs.title: CAN
docs.text: Pulsar Python SDK

docs.title: CAN
docs.text: Use PcpOverCan for a bus connected through one Pulsar USB-to-CAN adapter.

docs.title: Scan
docs.text:
LinuxWindows 
from pulsar_sdk import PcpOverCan

with PcpOverCan("/dev/ttyACM0") as can:
    print(can.scan())

from pulsar_sdk import PcpOverCan

with PcpOverCan("COM3") as can:
    print(can.scan())

The default scan range is 16–255. Actuator addresses must be unique within the domain and lie in 16–16382.

docs.title: Connect an actuator
docs.text:
LinuxWindows 
from pulsar_sdk import PcpOverCan, PulsarActuatorReal

can = PcpOverCan("/dev/ttyACM0")
actuator = PulsarActuatorReal(can, address=20)

from pulsar_sdk import PcpOverCan, PulsarActuatorReal

can = PcpOverCan("COM3")
actuator = PulsarActuatorReal(can, address=20)

Several actuators on the same bus must reuse the same PcpOverCan object.

docs.title: CAN bit-rate switching
docs.text:
set_can_brs_enabled() coordinates the setting across connected actuators while output is inactive:

with can:
    can.set_can_brs_enabled(True)

Treat BRS as a bus-wide configuration. All devices must be compatible and configured consistently.

docs.title: Capacity
docs.text:
More than eight registered actuators is permitted, but the SDK emits a telemetry-utilization warning. Select only required telemetry and estimate the bus load with the CAN bus utilization tool.

For multi-actuator composition, continue with Groups and platforms.

docs.title: Direct USB
docs.text: Pulsar Python SDK

docs.title: Direct USB
docs.text:
Use PcpOverUsb for one actuator connected directly to the computer. The actuator address must be 0.

from pulsar_sdk import PcpOverUsb, PulsarActuatorReal

usb = PcpOverUsb()  # Auto-detect when one Pulsar serial device is available.
actuator = PulsarActuatorReal(usb, address=0)

Pass a port when auto-detection is ambiguous:

LinuxWindows 
usb = PcpOverUsb("/dev/ttyACM0")

usb = PcpOverUsb("COM3")

docs.title: Complete short run
docs.text:
from time import sleep

from pulsar_sdk import ControlConfiguration, Mode, PcpOverUsb, PulsarActuatorReal

actuator = PulsarActuatorReal(PcpOverUsb(), address=0)
with actuator:
    actuator.configure(ControlConfiguration(Mode.VELOCITY))
    actuator.enable()
    actuator.set_command(1.0)
    sleep(2)
    actuator.disable()

See Direct USB hardware connectivity for wiring and Safety and prerequisites before running motion code.
